correctness.rationale: For every L,H>=1 and r>0, a capped-tooth backward recurrence with a reflecting tip yields the explicit impedance a_H. The backbone resolvent has decay exponent gamma_H and first-hitting Laplace transform exp(-L gamma_H); the renewal identity gives the exact reset mean. Expanding theta at r=u/L^4 while H/L^2->kappa>0 yields L^2(1-a_H)->sqrt(u)tanh(kappa sqrt(u)) and the claimed crossover. The two iterated endpoint limits follow from tanh expansions. The 21 independent numerical checks include a separately built finite Markov generator and tooth continued fractions; these are checks rather than proofs of the infinite limit.

value.rationale: The joint scaling H proportional to L squared is selected by the physical competition of return time from capped teeth (H squared) and backbone target search time (L to the fourth). The new explicit tanh interpolation is a complete quantitative reset-performance profile between normal and anomalous transport, not a routine finite enumeration or a simple change of model name.
